test_cases.test_name: Verify Configuration of End-to-End Workflow Templates
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system successfully configures and executes the defined end-to-end workflow templates covering apheresis, manufacturing, QC, and infusion stages.
prerequisites: System is fully installed and configured (GAMP Cat 4 baseline).
Test patient data set is available.
Workflow templates for Apheresis, Manufacturing Slotting, QC Release, and Infusion are loaded via vendor configuration.

test_steps.action: Initiate a new patient journey using the configured end-to-end workflow template.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully transitions the patient record through the Apheresis scheduling step.

test_steps.action: Advance the workflow through simulated manufacturing slot allocation and QC hold points.
test_steps.expected_result: The system correctly enforces the sequence and transitions between stages based on configured rules, logging all state changes.

test_steps.action: Complete the final Infusion step and verify final status.
test_steps.expected_result: The workflow completes successfully, and the final status is marked as 'Vein-to-Vein Complete'.

acceptance_criteria: The end-to-end workflow executes without manual intervention based solely on configuration.
All required workflow stages (URS-028-001) are successfully traversed.
data_integrity_requirements: Verify that all state transitions are recorded accurately in the audit trail.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Chain-of-Identity and Custody Dual-Scanning Enforcement
test_cases.objective: To confirm that the system strictly enforces Chain-of-Identity (CoI) and Chain-of-Custody (CoC) by requiring dual-scanning verification at critical handoffs.
prerequisites: System is operational.
Two unique physical identifiers (e.g., Patient ID, Sample ID) are available for testing.
Two functional barcode scanners integrated and configured.

test_steps.action: Attempt to advance the workflow from Apheresis collection to Logistics staging using only the first required scan (e.g., Patient ID).
test_steps.expected_result: The system blocks progression and displays an error message requiring the second scan (e.g., Sample ID).

test_steps.action: Perform the correct dual-scan sequence (Patient ID followed by Sample ID) at the Logistics staging point.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the input, logs both scan events with timestamps, and updates the custody record.
data_to_capture: Audit Trail entry for Custody Transfer

test_steps.action: Attempt to perform a custody transfer using an incorrect second scan (e.g., wrong Sample ID for the current patient).
test_steps.expected_result: The system rejects the transfer, flags a CoI mismatch, and generates a high-priority alert.

acceptance_criteria: Progression is strictly gated until both required identifiers are successfully scanned and matched (URS-028-002).
All successful and failed scan attempts are recorded in the audit trail (URS-028-008).
data_integrity_requirements: Verify that the audit trail captures the identity of the user, the scanner used, and the exact time of each scan event.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Configurable Constraint-Based Scheduling and Slot Allocation
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly enforces scheduling constraints and allocates manufacturing slots based on defined business rules.
prerequisites: System is fully installed and configured.
Test patient profiles with varying logistical constraints (e.g., distance, required temperature range) are available.
Scheduling constraints (e.g., max concurrent batches, facility capacity) are configured in the system.

test_steps.action: Input a new patient journey requiring an apheresis appointment and attempt to schedule it against a known full manufacturing slot capacity.
test_steps.expected_result: The system rejects the scheduling request and provides an error message indicating capacity constraint violation.
data_to_capture: System log entry for scheduling attempt

test_steps.action: Schedule a second patient journey that adheres to all configured constraints (e.g., required lead time, available slot).
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully allocates the required apheresis and manufacturing slots, updating the overall schedule dashboard.

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify the schedule for the second patient to violate a time-based constraint (e.g., moving the apheresis date too close to manufacturing start).
test_steps.expected_result: The system flags the modification as invalid or automatically adjusts the dependent steps to maintain compliance with constraints.

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully prevents scheduling when configured constraints are violated.
The system correctly allocates slots when all constraints are met.
All scheduling actions are recorded in the audit trail (URS-028-008).
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure scheduling data integrity across all linked modules (LIMS, MES).

test_cases.test_name: Verify Audit Trail and E-Signature Enforcement for Critical Handoffs
test_cases.objective: To confirm that all critical custody events and workflow handoffs are immutably recorded with associated e-signatures as required by regulatory standards.
prerequisites: System is configured for 21 CFR Part 11 compliance.
Test users with appropriate e-signature credentials are set up.
A complete, multi-step workflow (Apheresis -> Manufacturing Slotting -> QC Release) is ready for execution.

test_steps.action: Execute the 'QC Release' step in the workflow, which requires an authorized user e-signature.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prompts for the user's credentials and captures the electronic signature before allowing the status change.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail for the custody transfer event between the Logistics module and the MES module.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail entry clearly shows the 'from' system, the 'to' system, the timestamp, and the specific data elements transferred.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entry details for the handoff
Verification that the entry is non-modifiable

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify a critical data point (e.g., initial cell count) after it has been signed off by QC, without initiating a formal review/re-sign process.
test_steps.expected_result: The system prevents direct modification of the signed record, or forces a new version/review cycle with a subsequent e-signature.
data_to_capture: Audit log of the failed modification attempt

acceptance_criteria: All critical actions are protected by mandatory e-signatures (URS-028-009).
The audit trail captures all required custody and modification events comprehensively (URS-028-008).
Data integrity is maintained across workflow state transitions.
data_integrity_requirements: Verification of non-repudiation for all e-signatures.
Confirmation that audit logs meet GDP requirements for traceability.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Exception Handling for Temperature Excursions
test_cases.objective: Verify the system correctly triggers and manages the exception workflow for simulated cold-chain temperature excursions.
prerequisites: System configured with a valid logistics workflow template (URS-028-001).
A test sample/lot is active in the system.
Access to simulate a temperature alert from a connected monitoring device or manual input.

test_steps.action: Initiate the logistics tracking phase for the test sample.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays the sample in transit status.

test_steps.action: Simulate a temperature excursion event (e.g., input data indicating the sample went outside the defined acceptable range).
test_steps.expected_result: The system immediately halts the standard workflow progression and triggers the exception handling workflow (URS-028-004).

test_steps.action: Attempt to proceed to the next standard step (e.g., QC release) without resolving the exception.
test_steps.expected_result: The system blocks progression and requires documented disposition/resolution of the temperature excursion.

test_steps.action: Resolve the exception by applying a documented disposition (e.g., Quarantine/Reject) using an e-signature.
test_steps.expected_result: The exception workflow is closed, the disposition is recorded, and an audit trail entry is created (URS-028-008, URS-028-009).

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully intercepts the standard workflow upon temperature excursion.
The exception workflow (URS-028-004) is initiated and requires resolution.
Resolution requires an authorized e-signature (URS-028-009).
All steps are recorded in the audit trail (URS-028-008).
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure no data corruption occurs during workflow suspension/resumption.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Custom Algorithm Module Integration and Explainability
test_cases.objective: Verify that an optional, custom-developed algorithm module can be successfully integrated, executed for patient-to-lot matching, and that its decision artifacts are accessible.
prerequisites: The platform is deployed with containerization support (URS-028-015).
A containerized custom matching algorithm module (URS-028-006) is deployed and registered.
Test patient data and available manufacturing lot data are loaded.

test_steps.action: Initiate the patient-to-lot matching process, ensuring the configuration directs the system to use the custom algorithm module.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully calls the external containerized module.

test_steps.action: Review the output of the matching process.
test_steps.expected_result: The system returns a recommended match score and status based on the custom logic.

test_steps.action: Retrieve and review the explainability artifacts generated by the module for the specific matching decision.
test_steps.expected_result: The system provides artifacts detailing which input parameters drove the final matching decision (URS-028-016).
data_to_capture: Key factors listed in the explanation

test_steps.action: Attempt to execute the matching process using a configuration that bypasses the custom module (reverting to vendor scripting/rules).
test_steps.expected_result: The system executes the vendor-configured matching logic instead, confirming modularity.

acceptance_criteria: The custom module is successfully invoked via the orchestration layer.
The system correctly processes the output from the custom module.
Explainability artifacts (URS-028-016) are generated and retrievable for the decision.
The system correctly switches back to vendor configuration when the custom module is disabled.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure the custom module's output is correctly persisted and associated with the patient record.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Configurable Risk Scoring Rule Execution
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system correctly applies and executes configurable risk scoring rules based on defined parameters.
prerequisites: System is fully configured and operational.
Risk scoring rules (URS-028-005) are configured in the vendor scripting interface.
Test patient data sets simulating high-risk and low-risk scenarios are available.

test_steps.action: Input patient data set A (designed to trigger a high-risk score based on configured rules) into the orchestration platform.
test_steps.expected_result: The system calculates and assigns the expected high-risk score, triggering the associated workflow exception path.

test_steps.action: Input patient data set B (designed to trigger a low-risk score) into the orchestration platform.
test_steps.expected_result: The system calculates and assigns the expected low-risk score, allowing the process to proceed to the next standard step.

test_steps.action: Review the audit trail for both transactions to confirm the risk score calculation and decision point are logged.
test_steps.expected_result: Audit trail (URS-028-008) accurately reflects the input parameters, the calculated score, and the resulting workflow decision.
data_to_capture: Audit log entries for both transactions

acceptance_criteria: The system accurately calculates risk scores according to the configured vendor scripting rules.
The resulting workflow path aligns with the defined risk score thresholds.
data_integrity_requirements: Risk score calculation must be immutable in the audit log.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Integration with External Systems (EHR/LIMS/Courier)
test_cases.objective: To verify successful, secure, and timely data exchange between the Orchestration Platform and required external systems (EHR, LIMS, Courier) via configured APIs.
prerequisites: Test instances of EHR, LIMS, and Courier systems are available and configured for integration testing.
API credentials and connection parameters are loaded into the platform.
SSO/OIDC (URS-028-014) is functional for user access.

test_steps.action: Initiate a new patient journey requiring data input from the EHR system (e.g., patient demographics).
test_steps.expected_result: The platform successfully authenticates via OIDC/SSO and retrieves the required patient data from the EHR API within the latency requirement.

test_steps.action: Advance the workflow to the manufacturing slotting stage, requiring data submission to the LIMS system.
test_steps.expected_result: The platform successfully transmits the required manufacturing order details to the LIMS system, and LIMS confirms receipt/slot allocation.

test_steps.action: Trigger a logistics event requiring shipment notification to the courier system, including chain-of-custody data.
test_steps.expected_result: The platform sends the shipment manifest and custody transfer details to the courier API, and the courier system acknowledges the creation of the shipment record.
data_to_capture: GDP compliance data points transferred (e.g., temperature log headers)

test_steps.action: Verify that all data transfers are logged in the platform's audit trail.
test_steps.expected_result: Audit logs confirm successful API calls, response codes, and timestamps for all three external system interactions.

acceptance_criteria: All required data exchanges with EHR, LIMS, and Courier systems are successful.
API response times meet the performance requirement of < 1 second latency for event processing (URS-028-012).
Data integrity is maintained across all integration points.
data_integrity_requirements: Data mapping accuracy between systems must be 100% verified.

test_cases.test_name: Verify SSO and Device Identity Integration for Scanners
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system successfully enforces Single Sign-On (SSO) via OIDC and validates device identity for all connected scanning hardware.
prerequisites: OIDC Provider configured and reachable.
Test scanners provisioned with valid device identities.
User accounts configured for SSO access.

test_steps.action: Attempt to log into the platform using a standard user account via the OIDC portal.
test_steps.expected_result: User is successfully authenticated and granted access based on role permissions.

test_steps.action: Attempt to perform a critical custody scan (e.g., material receipt) using a scanner whose device identity is unregistered or invalid.
test_steps.expected_result: The system rejects the scan event, displaying an error indicating device identity failure.

test_steps.action: Perform a critical custody scan using a valid, registered scanner.
test_steps.expected_result: The scan is accepted, and the custody event is recorded successfully in the audit trail.

acceptance_criteria: Successful authentication via OIDC is confirmed.
Unauthorized scanners are blocked from executing custody transactions.
Authorized scanners successfully record custody events.
data_integrity_requirements: Verify that failed device authentications do not result in phantom custody records.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Performance Under Concurrent Load for Orchestration
test_cases.objective: To verify the system's ability to orchestrate 1,000 concurrent patient journeys while maintaining required event processing latency.
prerequisites: Load testing environment configured to simulate 1,000 active patient journeys.
Monitoring tools active to capture system metrics (CPU, memory, latency).

test_steps.action: Initiate the load test script designed to simulate 1,000 concurrent, active patient workflows (covering apheresis scheduling through QC release handoff).
test_steps.expected_result: All 1,000 workflows are successfully initiated without system crash or deadlock.

test_steps.action: Monitor the system for a defined period (e.g., 15 minutes) while the load is sustained.
test_steps.expected_result: No critical errors or timeouts are recorded in the system logs.

test_steps.action: Measure the average and 95th percentile latency for key orchestration events (e.g., LIMS result receipt triggering the next workflow step) across the 1,000 journeys.
test_steps.expected_result: The average event processing latency is less than 1 second, and the 95th percentile latency is acceptable (e.g., < 2 seconds).

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully manages 1,000 concurrent journeys.
Event processing latency meets the URS requirement of < 1 second under normal load (as defined by the test profile).
data_integrity_requirements: Verify that all 1,000 journeys complete without data corruption or loss of custody events.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Dashboard KPI Reporting for Vein-to-Vein Time
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system accurately calculates and displays key performance indicators (KPIs) related to vein-to-vein time on the designated dashboard.
prerequisites: System is fully configured and operational.
At least three complete, successful patient journeys (apheresis to infusion) have been processed.
Access to the KPI dashboard interface is available.

test_steps.action: Initiate three distinct patient workflows, ensuring accurate timestamps are recorded for apheresis start, manufacturing slot assignment, QC release, and final infusion.
test_steps.expected_result: All workflow steps are successfully logged with associated timestamps.
data_to_capture: Start/End timestamps for each major phase

test_steps.action: Navigate to the KPI dashboard and locate the 'Vein-to-Vein Time' metric.
test_steps.expected_result: The dashboard loads successfully, displaying calculated metrics.

test_steps.action: Manually calculate the vein-to-vein time for the three processed patients using the raw audit log data (Apheresis Start to Infusion End).
test_steps.expected_result: Manual calculation is complete.

test_steps.action: Compare the system-reported vein-to-vein time KPIs against the manually calculated times for all three patients.
test_steps.expected_result: The system-reported KPIs match the manually calculated times within an acceptable tolerance (e.g., +/- 1 second).

acceptance_criteria: The KPI dashboard accurately reflects the vein-to-vein time based on logged workflow events.
KPIs for release metrics (e.g., QC release rate) are also present and verifiable.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure timestamp accuracy across the workflow engine.

test_cases.test_name: Verify GDP Compliance for Cold-Chain Custody Records
test_cases.objective: Verify that temperature excursion data captured during logistics handoffs is correctly recorded, linked to the patient/lot identity, and compliant with GDP requirements.
prerequisites: System is configured to receive temperature data from logistics monitoring devices.
A simulated cold-chain shipment path involving at least two custody transfers is defined.

test_steps.action: Simulate a logistics transfer where the temperature sensor reports a minor excursion (e.g., 2 degrees above the upper limit) during the transit phase.
test_steps.expected_result: The system flags the event and generates a temperature excursion alert.

test_steps.action: Verify that the temperature excursion record is directly linked via audit trail to the specific Chain-of-Custody event (hand-off) and the associated patient/lot ID.
test_steps.expected_result: The audit trail clearly shows the custody transfer event immediately preceding or concurrent with the excursion logging.
data_to_capture: Audit trail entries for custody and excursion

test_steps.action: Access the final custody record (e.g., prior to manufacturing receipt) and confirm that the excursion data is immutable and available for review.
test_steps.expected_result: The record confirms the excursion occurred, and no manual modification of the excursion data is possible.

test_steps.action: Verify that the system generates a reportable record of the excursion suitable for GDP compliance review.
test_steps.expected_result: A report can be generated showing the excursion details, linked to URS-028-010.

acceptance_criteria: Temperature excursion data is accurately captured and associated with the correct custody event.
The system enforces GDP requirements by preventing alteration of cold-chain records.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure time synchronization between external sensors and the platform.
Verify immutability of temperature logs.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Containerization and Versioning of Custom Algorithm Modules
test_cases.objective: Verify that optional custom algorithm modules can be successfully deployed, containerized, and versioned within the orchestration platform.
prerequisites: Custom Algorithm Module (v1.0) is developed and containerized (e.g., Docker image).
Platform access with permissions to deploy custom modules.
Configuration exists to optionally enable the custom module.

test_steps.action: Deploy the containerized Custom Algorithm Module (v1.0) to the platform environment.
test_steps.expected_result: The platform successfully registers and recognizes the module, associating it with version 1.0.
data_to_capture: Platform configuration record for Module v1.0

test_steps.action: Activate a workflow that utilizes the newly deployed Custom Algorithm Module (v1.0) for patient-to-lot matching.
test_steps.expected_result: The workflow executes successfully, and the matching decision reflects the logic of Module v1.0.

test_steps.action: Deploy an updated version (v1.1) of the Custom Algorithm Module, replacing v1.0.
test_steps.expected_result: The platform successfully updates the module reference to v1.1, and the system retains the ability to reference the historical v1.0 version if required for rollback or audit.
data_to_capture: System inventory showing active version v1.1

acceptance_criteria: Custom modules are successfully deployed and recognized by the orchestration engine.
The system correctly identifies and utilizes the active version of the custom module.
The platform maintains version control artifacts for deployed modules (URS-028-015).
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure versioning prevents accidental execution of incorrect module logic.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Latency Compliance Under Peak Load Conditions
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system maintains event processing latency below 1 second while orchestrating 1,000 concurrent patient journeys.
prerequisites: Test environment configured to simulate 1,000 concurrent patient journeys (e.g., through automated load generation).
Monitoring tools configured to capture timestamped event processing times.

test_steps.action: Initiate the load test, simulating the start of 1,000 unique patient workflows simultaneously.
test_steps.expected_result: All 1,000 workflows are successfully initiated without system failure or queuing backlog.

test_steps.action: Monitor key orchestration events (e.g., status updates, handoffs between systems) across the 1,000 concurrent journeys.
test_steps.expected_result: The system processes events continuously without significant degradation in throughput.

test_steps.action: Analyze the recorded timestamps for a statistically significant sample (e.g., 100) of critical workflow events.
test_steps.expected_result: The 95th percentile latency for critical event processing is less than 1.0 second (URS-028-012).

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully manages 1,000 concurrent patient journeys (URS-028-011).
Event processing latency remains below the 1-second threshold under this load (URS-028-012).
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure load generation does not corrupt timestamps or event sequencing.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Configuration of Risk Scoring Rules Using Vendor Scripting
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system correctly applies and executes configurable risk scoring rules defined via vendor scripting capabilities.
prerequisites: System is fully installed and configured.
Access to the configuration interface for risk scoring rules.
Test patient data sets representing low, medium, and high-risk scenarios are prepared.

test_steps.action: Configure a specific risk scoring rule (e.g., 'High Risk if Delay > 4h AND Temp < 2C') using the vendor scripting tool.
test_steps.expected_result: The rule is saved, validated by the system, and activated for use in the workflow.
data_to_capture: Rule ID and configuration script hash.

test_steps.action: Submit a test patient journey matching the 'High Risk' criteria defined in Step 1.
test_steps.expected_result: The orchestration platform assigns the corresponding high-risk score and triggers the appropriate exception workflow (URS-028-004).

test_steps.action: Submit a test patient journey matching a 'Low Risk' scenario.
test_steps.expected_result: The system assigns a low risk score and proceeds along the standard path without triggering exception handling.

acceptance_criteria: All configured risk scoring rules execute accurately based on input parameters.
The system correctly branches the workflow based on the calculated risk score.
data_integrity_requirements: Risk score calculation must be logged in the audit trail.

test_cases.test_name: Verify Explainability Artifacts for Custom Algorithm Decisions
test_cases.objective: Verify that when a custom-developed algorithm module is used for patient-to-lot matching, the system generates and retains required explainability artifacts.
prerequisites: A custom algorithm module (URS-028-006) is deployed and containerized (URS-028-015).
A patient journey requiring the custom matching algorithm is initiated.

test_steps.action: Initiate a patient journey that requires the custom algorithm module to perform patient-to-lot matching optimization.
test_steps.expected_result: The custom module executes successfully, and a matching decision is recorded.
data_to_capture: Patient ID and Lot ID matched.

test_steps.action: Access the record associated with the matching decision made in Step 1.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays or allows retrieval of the explainability artifacts generated by the custom module (e.g., feature importance, decision path).
data_to_capture: Content snapshot of the explainability report.

test_steps.action: Verify that the retrieved artifacts align with the logic implemented in the custom module version.
test_steps.expected_result: The explanation confirms the key inputs that led to the specific matching decision.

acceptance_criteria: Explainability artifacts are generated for every decision made by the custom algorithm module.
Artifacts are traceable to the specific module version used (URS-028-015).
regulatory_basis: General principles of data integrity and traceability for critical algorithms.
data_integrity_requirements: Explainability artifacts must be immutable and retained for the required retention period.

test_cases.test_name: Verify System Resilience During 1000 Concurrent Patient Journey Orchestrations
test_cases.objective: To verify the system's ability to successfully orchestrate 1,000 concurrent patient journeys without failure or significant degradation.
prerequisites: System configured for production load simulation.
Load testing tools configured to simulate 1,000 active patient workflows.
Monitoring tools active to track resource utilization.

test_steps.action: Initiate the load test script designed to start 1,000 unique, end-to-end patient workflows simultaneously.
test_steps.expected_result: All 1,000 workflows are successfully initiated and progress through the initial configuration steps (apheresis scheduling, slot allocation).

test_steps.action: Monitor the system for a defined period (e.g., 30 minutes) while the workflows progress through manufacturing and QC stages.
test_steps.expected_result: All 1,000 workflows complete their defined path or reach a stable state without crashing or entering unrecoverable errors.
data_to_capture: Workflow completion status for all 1,000 instances
Error logs generated during the test period

test_steps.action: Review the system logs and performance metrics post-test.
test_steps.expected_result: No critical system failures or resource exhaustion events are recorded, confirming stability under maximum specified load.

acceptance_criteria: URS-028-011: The system successfully orchestrates 1,000 concurrent patient journeys.
No workflow instances fail due to resource contention or orchestration errors.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure no data corruption occurs across the concurrent workflows.

test_cases.test_name: Verify GDP Compliance for Custody Events Under Exception Conditions
test_cases.objective: To verify that the system maintains accurate chain-of-custody records and enforces GDP requirements even when workflow exceptions (e.g., delays) are triggered.
prerequisites: System configured with active workflow templates.
Test materials prepared for custody transfer simulation.
Ability to manually trigger a simulated delay/temperature excursion event.

test_steps.action: Initiate a patient workflow and simulate a critical custody handoff (e.g., Apheresis to Logistics transfer).
test_steps.expected_result: The system prompts for dual-scanning verification (URS-028-002) and records the custody transfer timestamp.

test_steps.action: While the material is in transit (simulated), trigger a pre-configured exception, such as a 4-hour delay or a minor temperature excursion alert.
test_steps.expected_result: The system triggers the exception handling workflow (URS-028-004) and flags the custody record appropriately.

test_steps.action: Complete the custody transfer and review the audit trail and custody log for the affected material.
test_steps.expected_result: The final custody record accurately reflects the delay/excursion event, the corrective actions taken (if any), and maintains an immutable audit trail linking the exception to the custody transfer, satisfying GDP logging requirements.
data_to_capture: Final audit trail entry for the custody event
GDP compliance report snippet for the material ID

acceptance_criteria: URS-028-004: Exception handling workflows are correctly triggered by the exception event.
URS-028-008 & URS-028-010: The audit trail immutably records the custody event, including the impact of the exception, meeting GDP logging standards.
data_integrity_requirements: Ensure the integrity of the custody chain is maintained and documented despite the exception.

test_cases.test_name: Verify E2E Workflow Execution with EHR/LIMS Data Input
test_cases.objective: Verify the platform successfully orchestrates a complete patient journey, starting from EHR data input through LIMS scheduling.
prerequisites: System configured with valid API credentials for EHR and LIMS.
A test patient record created in the EHR system.
A valid workflow template (URS-028-001) is active.

test_steps.action: Initiate a new patient journey by pushing required demographic and clinical data from the simulated EHR system into the Orchestration Platform.
test_steps.expected_result: The platform successfully ingests the data and automatically triggers the first step of the configured workflow (e.g., Apheresis Scheduling).

test_steps.action: Verify that the platform successfully calls the LIMS integration to reserve a manufacturing slot based on the patient profile and constraints.
test_steps.expected_result: A manufacturing slot is confirmed and recorded in the platform, and the workflow advances to the logistics scheduling step.

test_steps.action: Review the Audit Trail (URS-028-008) for the entire sequence of automated steps.
test_steps.expected_result: All data handoffs between the platform and integrated systems (EHR, LIMS) are accurately logged with timestamps and user/system context.
data_to_capture: Audit log entries for integration points.

acceptance_criteria: The end-to-end workflow executes successfully from EHR input to slot reservation without manual intervention.
All integration points log data correctly per URS-028-008.
data_integrity_requirements: Data integrity must be maintained across all system boundaries during integration.

test_cases.test_name: Verify E-Signature Enforcement on Critical Release Action
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system strictly enforces 21 CFR Part 11 compliant e-signatures for the final QC release step before proceeding to infusion.
prerequisites: A test patient journey is progressed to the QC Release step.
Two distinct user accounts (Reviewer and Approver) are available.
System configured for Part 11 compliance (URS-028-009).

test_steps.action: Attempt to transition the patient journey from 'QC Pending' to 'Released' without providing any credentials.
test_steps.expected_result: The system blocks the transition and displays an error requiring authentication/signature.

test_steps.action: Attempt to sign the release using the credentials of the 'Reviewer' user, who is not authorized for final release.
test_steps.expected_result: The system rejects the signature, logs the failed attempt in the audit trail, and prevents workflow progression.
data_to_capture: Audit log entry for failed signature attempt.

test_steps.action: Successfully execute the e-signature process using the authorized 'Approver' credentials, confirming the release.
test_steps.expected_result: The workflow advances to the 'Infusion Scheduled' state, and the audit trail captures the complete signature record (ID, date, time, meaning).
data_to_capture: E-signature record details captured in the audit trail.

acceptance_criteria: The system prevents unauthorized or incomplete e-signatures from advancing the critical workflow step.
A complete, compliant e-signature record is generated and immutable in the audit trail upon successful release.
data_integrity_requirements: Strict enforcement of electronic signature controls to ensure data authenticity.
